nodes.summary: For every cell $o$ over the non-blank symbols of an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$, the cell symbol of $o$ is $b$ when $o$ is the blank cell and is $x$ when $o$ holds the non-blank symbol $x$.
nodes.title: Value of the cell-symbol map

nodes.summary: Distinct cells over the non-blank symbols of an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ have distinct cell symbols in $\Gamma_0$.
nodes.title: The cell-symbol map is injective

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet with blank symbol $b$. A tape cell over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ is either blank or holds a symbol $x \ne b$ of $\Gamma_0$. Its cell symbol is $b$ for the blank cell and $x$ for the cell holding $x$. This map from cells to $\Gamma_0$ sends the blank cell to the blank symbol, so it is a pointed map.
nodes.title: Cell symbol

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be a finite alphabet with at least one non-blank symbol, let $M$ be a Post–Turing machine over $\Gamma_0$ supported by the finite set of states $S$, and let $l$ be a word of non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$. The single-tape machine simulating $M$ halts on the input $l$ if and only if $M$, started on $l$, halts.
nodes.title: The simulating machine halts exactly when the Post–Turing machine halts

nodes.summary: For every stack tape $s$ over $\Gamma$ (a finite list of cells, each a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank, that does not end in a blank), the first cell of the half-tape view of $s$ (its cells followed by infinitely many blanks) is the first cell of $s$, which is the blank if $s$ is empty.
nodes.title: First cell of the half-tape view of a stack tape

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet with blank symbol $b$. For every stack tape $s$ of cells over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ (a finite list of cells, blank beyond its end), the first symbol of the half-tape over $\Gamma_0$ read from $s$ is the cell symbol of the first cell of $s$; when $s$ is empty this is $b$.
nodes.title: First symbol of a half-tape read from non-blank cells

nodes.summary: For every two-way tape $t$ over $\Gamma$ (a head cell with a left and a right stack tape), the head cell of the view of $t$ as a tape of cells is the head cell of $t$.
nodes.title: Head cell of the view of a two-way tape

nodes.summary: For every two-way tape $t$ of cells over the non-blank symbols of an alphabet $\Gamma_0$, the symbol under the head of the tape over $\Gamma_0$ read from $t$ is the cell symbol of the cell under the head of $t$.
nodes.title: Head symbol of a tape read from non-blank cells

nodes.summary: For every two-way tape $t$ over $\Gamma$ (a head cell with a left and a right stack tape), the left half of the view of $t$ as a tape of cells is the half-tape view of the left stack tape of $t$.
nodes.title: Left half of the view of a two-way tape

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with a distinguished blank symbol $b$, the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ are the elements $x \in \Gamma_0$ with $x \ne b$. They form the tape alphabet of the single-tape machine that simulates a Post–Turing machine over $\Gamma_0$.
nodes.title: Non-blank symbols

nodes.summary: For every stack tape $s$ over $\Gamma$ (a finite list of cells, each a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank, that does not end in a blank) and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the cell at position $n$ of the half-tape view of $s$ (its cells followed by infinitely many blanks) is the $n$-th cell of $s$, counting from $0$, if $n$ is less than the length of $s$, and the blank otherwise.
nodes.title: Cells of the half-tape view of a stack tape

nodes.summary: For every word $w = w_0 \cdots w_{m-1}$ over $\Gamma$ and every integer $i$, the cell at position $i$ of the view of the input tape of $w$ is $w_i$ if $0 \le i < m$, and the blank otherwise.
nodes.title: Cells of an input tape

nodes.summary: For every two-way tape $t$ over $\Gamma$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every integer $i$, the cell at position $i$ of the view of the tape obtained from $t$ by moving the head $n$ times to the right is the cell at position $i + n$ of the view of $t$.
nodes.title: Cells after $n$ moves to the right

nodes.summary: For an optional direction $d$, let $\delta(d)$ be $0$ if $d$ is no move, $-1$ if $d$ is a move to the left and $1$ if $d$ is a move to the right. For every two-way tape $t$ over $\Gamma$ and every integer $i$, the cell at position $i$ of the view of the tape obtained from $t$ by the optional move $d$ is the cell at position $i + \delta(d)$ of the view of $t$.
nodes.title: Cells after an optional move

nodes.summary: For an optional direction $d$, let $\delta(d)$ be $0$ if $d$ is no move, $-1$ if $d$ is a move to the left and $1$ if $d$ is a move to the right. For every two-way tape $t$ over $\Gamma$, every cell $a$ (a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank) and every integer $i$, the cell at position $i$ of the view of the tape obtained from $t$ by writing $a$ under the head and then performing the optional move $d$ is $a$ if…
nodes.title: Cells after a write and an optional move

nodes.summary: For every two-way tape $t$ over $\Gamma$, every cell $a$ (a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank) and every integer $i$, the cell at position $i$ of the view of the tape obtained from $t$ by writing $a$ under the head is $a$ if $i = 0$, and the cell at position $i$ of the view of $t$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Cells after a write

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a two-way tape over $\Gamma$ with head cell $h$, left stack tape $(\ell_0, \dots, \ell_{p-1})$ and right stack tape $(r_0, \dots, r_{q-1})$. For every integer $i$, the cell at position $i$ of the view of $t$ as a tape of cells is $h$ if $i = 0$, $r_{i-1}$ if $0 < i \le q$, $\ell_{-i-1}$ if $-p \le i < 0$, and the blank otherwise.
nodes.title: The cells of the view

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be a finite alphabet with blank symbol $b$ and at least one non-blank symbol, and let $M$ be a Post–Turing machine over $\Gamma_0$ with start state $q_0$, supported by the finite set of states $S$ (so $q_0 \in S$, and from a state in $S$ the machine $M$ only enters states in $S$). The single-tape machine simulating $M$ has the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ as tape alphabet, $S$ as set of states and…
nodes.title: Single-tape simulation of a Post–Turing machine

nodes.summary: For every optional head move $d$ (no move, a move to the left, or a move to the right), the offset of $d$ lies between $-1$ and $1$, that is, $-1 \le \mathrm{offset}(d) \le 1$.
nodes.title: The offset of an optional move is at most one

nodes.summary: The offset of an optional head move $d$ is $0$ if $d$ is no move, $-1$ if $d$ is a move to the left and $1$ if $d$ is a move to the right.
nodes.title: Offset of an optional head move

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be a finite alphabet with at least one non-blank symbol, let $M$ be a Post–Turing machine over $\Gamma_0$ supported by the finite set of states $S$, and let $l$ and $l'$ be words of non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$. If $M$, started on $l$, halts in a configuration whose tape holds $l'$ starting at the head, with blanks everywhere else, then the single-tape machine simulating $M$ outputs $l'$ on the…
nodes.title: The single-tape simulation has the same output

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be a finite alphabet with at least one non-blank symbol, let $M$ be a Post–Turing machine over $\Gamma_0$ supported by the finite set of states $S$, and let $l$ and $l'$ be words of non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$. If $M$, started on $l$, reaches in exactly $n$ steps a configuration $c$ in which it halts, and the tape of $c$ holds $l'$ starting at the head with blanks everywhere else, then the…
nodes.title: The single-tape simulation outputs within one extra step

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a TM0 machine over a finite alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$ and at least one non-blank symbol, supported by a finite set $S$ of states, and let $\widehat{M}$ be the single-tape machine over the non-blank symbols $N = \Gamma_0 \setminus \{b\}$ simulating $M$. For a tape $t$ over $N$, write $\tau(t)$ for the TM0 tape read from $t$ cell by cell. If $M$ goes from a configuration $(q, T)$ to a…
nodes.title: Runs of a TM0 machine are runs of its single-tape simulation

nodes.summary: For every two-sided tape $t$ over $\Gamma$ (a head cell together with a left and a right stack tape), the right half of the tape view of $t$ is the half-tape view of the right half of $t$.
nodes.title: Right half of the tape view

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a TM0 machine over a finite alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$ and at least one non-blank symbol, supported by a finite set $S$ of states, and let $\widehat{M}$ be the single-tape machine over the non-blank symbols $N = \Gamma_0 \setminus \{b\}$ simulating $M$. For a tape $t$ over $N$, write $\tau(t)$ for the TM0 tape read from $t$ cell by cell. If $q \in S$ and $M$ has no step from the…
nodes.title: The simulation halts one step after the TM0 machine

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a TM0 machine over a finite alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$ and at least one non-blank symbol, supported by a finite set $S$ of states, and let $\widehat{M}$ be the single-tape machine over the non-blank symbols $N = \Gamma_0 \setminus \{b\}$ simulating $M$. For a tape $t$ over $N$, write $\tau(t)$ for the TM0 tape read from $t$ cell by cell. If $q \in S$ and one step of $M$ takes the…
nodes.title: Each TM0 step is one step of the simulation

nodes.summary: For every stack tape $s$ over $\Gamma$ (a list of cells, each a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank cell, not ending in a blank cell), the tail of the half-tape view of $s$ is the half-tape view of the tail of $s$: dropping the first cell of $s$ drops the first cell of its half-tape.
nodes.title: Tail of the half-tape view of a stack tape

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$ and every stack tape $s$ over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$, dropping the first symbol of the half-tape read from $s$ gives the half-tape read from $s$ with its first cell removed (the empty stack tape staying empty).
nodes.title: Dropping the first cell of a stack tape of non-blank symbols

nodes.summary: A stack tape $s$ over an alphabet $\Gamma$ is a finite list of cells, each a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank cell, that does not end in a blank cell. Its half-tape view is the half-tape of cells (a sequence of cells taken up to trailing blanks, the blank cell being the default) whose cells are those of $s$ in order, followed by blank cells.
nodes.title: Half-tape view of a stack tape

nodes.summary: For every cell $c$ (a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank cell) and every stack tape $s$ over $\Gamma$, the half-tape view of the stack tape obtained by pushing $c$ onto $s$ is the half-tape view of $s$ with $c$ pushed onto its front.
nodes.title: Pushing a cell onto a stack tape

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet with blank symbol $b$ and $N = \Gamma_0 \setminus \{b\}$. Read a cell over $N$ as a symbol of $\Gamma_0$: $b$ for the blank cell, $x$ for a cell holding $x$. For every cell $o$ and every stack tape $s$ over $N$, the half-tape read from the stack tape obtained by pushing $o$ onto $s$ is the half-tape read from $s$ with the symbol of $o$ pushed onto its front.
nodes.title: Pushing a cell onto a stack tape of non-blank symbols

nodes.summary: If two stack tapes over $\Gamma$ have the same half-tape view, then they are equal.
nodes.title: The half-tape view of stack tapes is injective

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$, two stack tapes over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ that read as the same half-tape over $\Gamma_0$ are equal.
nodes.title: Distinct stack tapes of non-blank symbols read as distinct half-tapes

nodes.summary: For every word $a_1 \cdots a_n$ over $\Gamma$, the half-tape view of the stack tape whose cells are the non-blank cells $a_1, \dots, a_n$ is the half-tape whose first $n$ cells are $a_1, \dots, a_n$ and whose later cells are blank.
nodes.title: Half-tape view of a word

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$ and a word $w$ of non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$, the half-tape read from the stack tape whose cells hold the letters of $w$ in order is the half-tape of $w$, viewed as a word over $\Gamma_0$.
nodes.title: A word of non-blank symbols reads as itself

nodes.summary: The half-tape view of the empty stack tape over $\Gamma$ is the half-tape all of whose cells are blank.
nodes.title: Half-tape view of the empty stack tape

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$, the empty stack tape over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ reads as the half-tape of the empty list, all of whose symbols are $b$.
nodes.title: The empty stack tape reads as the blank half-tape

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet with blank symbol $b$ and $N = \Gamma_0 \setminus \{b\}$ its non-blank symbols. A stack tape $s$ over $N$, a finite list of cells each blank or holding a symbol of $N$ and not ending in a blank cell, is read as the TM0 half-tape over $\Gamma_0$ whose $i$-th symbol is that of the $i$-th cell of $s$: $b$ for a blank cell, $x$ for a cell holding $x$, and $b$ past the end of $s$.
nodes.title: Half-tape of a stack tape of non-blank symbols

nodes.summary: A CSLib tape $t$ over an alphabet $\Gamma$ has a head cell and two halves, each a finite list of cells not ending in a blank, where a cell is a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank. Its cell view is the Mathlib tape over cells, with the blank as default symbol, whose head is the head cell of $t$ and whose left and right halves are the halves of $t$, blank past their ends. So the cell at position $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ of…
nodes.title: Cell view of a two-way tape

nodes.summary: If two two-sided tapes $t$ and $t'$ over $\Gamma$ (each a head cell together with a left and a right stack tape) have the same tape view as a tape of cells, then $t = t'$.
nodes.title: The tape view is injective

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$, two tapes over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ that read, cell by cell, as the same TM0 tape over $\Gamma_0$ are equal.
nodes.title: Distinct tapes of non-blank symbols read as distinct TM0 tapes

nodes.summary: For every word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{n-1}$ over $\Gamma$, the cell view of the input tape of $w$ is the Mathlib input tape of the list of non-blank cells $w_0, \dots, w_{n-1}$: the head is on $w_0$, the letters $w_1, \dots, w_{n-1}$ lie to its right in order, and every other cell is blank (for the empty word, every cell is blank).
nodes.title: The cell view of an input tape

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet whose default symbol is the blank. For every word $l$ of non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$, the Post–Turing reading of the two-way input tape of $l$ (the head on the first symbol of $l$, the rest of $l$ to its right, every other cell blank) is the Post–Turing machine input tape of $l$ read as a word over $\Gamma_0$, with the head on the first symbol of $l$ and the rest of $l$ to its right.
nodes.title: The Post–Turing reading of an input tape

nodes.summary: For every tape $t$ and each direction $d$ (left or right), the cell view of the tape obtained from $t$ by moving the head one cell in direction $d$ equals the tape obtained from the cell view of $t$ by moving its head one cell in direction $d$.
nodes.title: The cell view commutes with head moves

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet whose default symbol is the blank, and for a two-way tape $t$ whose cells are blank or hold non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$, let $\tau(t)$ be the Post–Turing reading of $t$, a Post–Turing machine tape over $\Gamma_0$. For every such $t$ and every direction $d$, left or right, $\tau$ of $t$ with its head moved in direction $d$ is $\tau(t)$ with its head moved in direction $d$.
nodes.title: Head moves commute with the Post–Turing reading of a tape

nodes.summary: For every two-way tape $t$ over $\Gamma$ and every optional head move $d$, which is either no move or a move one cell in a direction, the cell view of the tape obtained from $t$ by the optional move $d$ is the cell view of $t$ when $d$ is no move, and the cell view of $t$ with its head moved one cell in direction $d$ when $d$ is a direction.
nodes.title: The cell view commutes with optional head moves

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet whose default symbol is the blank, and for a two-way tape $t$ whose cells are blank or hold non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$, let $\tau(t)$ be the Post–Turing reading of $t$, a Post–Turing machine tape over $\Gamma_0$. For every such $t$ and every optional move $d$, which is either no move or a direction, $\tau$ of $t$ after the optional move $d$ is $\tau(t)$ when $d$ is no move, and…
nodes.title: Optional head moves commute with the Post–Turing reading of a tape

nodes.summary: For every tape $t$ and every cell $a$ (a symbol or the blank), the cell view of the tape obtained from $t$ by writing $a$ under the head equals the tape obtained from the cell view of $t$ by writing $a$ under its head.
nodes.title: The cell view commutes with writing

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet whose default symbol is the blank, and for a two-way tape $t$ whose cells are blank or hold non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$, let $\tau(t)$ be the Post–Turing reading of $t$, a Post–Turing machine tape over $\Gamma_0$. For every such $t$ and every cell $o$, blank or holding a non-blank symbol, $\tau$ of $t$ with $o$ written under the head is $\tau(t)$ with the symbol of $o$ written…
nodes.title: Writing commutes with the Post–Turing reading of a tape

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet whose default symbol is the blank. The Post–Turing reading of a two-way tape $t$ whose cells are blank or hold non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ is the Post–Turing machine tape over $\Gamma_0$ obtained cell by cell: take the view of $t$ as a tape of cells, each cell at its position relative to the head and blank cells past the ends, and replace each cell by its symbol, a non-blank symbol…
nodes.title: Post–Turing reading of a tape over the non-blank symbols
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
